content:
Hey everyone, I'm excited to share Pythagoras-Prover, a compute-efficient family of open-source theorem provers for Lean — including:
:small_blue_diamond: Pythagoras-Prover-4B — the smallest theorem prover to date
:small_blue_diamond: Pythagoras-Prover-Diffusion-4B — the first proof-of-concept diffusion-based theorem prover
With efficient LoRA training and an 8,192-token context length, Pythagoras-Prover reaches strong MiniF2F results with far smaller models.

:trophy: Results on MiniF2F
• Pythagoras-Prover-4B achieves 86.1% Pass@32, outperforming DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B at ~167× fewer parameters
• Pythagoras-Prover-32B reaches 89.8% Pass@32 and 92.6% Pass@2048 — the best MiniF2F result reported to date

:fixing: What's behind it
:puzzle_piece: A compute-frugal synthetic data pipeline: a Lean-verified corpus stratified into easy, medium, and hard tiers, trained with a difficulty curriculum so small models learn proof skills progressively, paired with a dynamic proof-reasoning filtering scheme that keeps informative long reasoning chains within a tight context budget
:sparkles: Augmented Lean Formalisation (ALF): a way to augment Lean formalisations at scale without per-instance verification, removing the dominant cost of formal data generation and helping address the scarcity of open-source Lean data — and reused via self-distillation to push both the 4B and 32B provers to state-of-the-art
:search: MiniF2F-ALF: a perturbed variant of MiniF2F that reopens a saturating benchmark, diversifies the failure modes, and better separates strong systems
:high_voltage: A diffusion proof of concept: we identify what holds diffusion provers back (sparse masking signal, limited stable context, scarce diffusion-ready data), mitigate it with tactic-based masking + ALF, and generate proofs 2.58× faster than the autoregressive counterpart

:earth_asia: Website:  https://pythagoras-lm.github.io/
:document: arXiv: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.12594
:fire: Models: https://huggingface.co/Pythagoras-LM
:magnifying_glass_tilted_right: X post: https://x.com/joshuaongg21/status/2066557451118485856?s=20

:key: Our models, data, and training pipeline will be released gradually soon.
Just to understand: do you write "theorem prover" in the sense of an agent that can autoformalise results expressed in natural language and/or formal language?

Hi, thanks so much for your interest in Pythagoras-Prover! In this work, we use “theorem prover” to refer to a foundation-model-style neural Lean prover: it takes formal Lean statements and generates formally checkable Lean proofs, rather than acting as an end-to-end agent for autoformalising natural-language mathematics.
This topic was moved here from #general > Pythagoras-Prover: Compute-Efficient Lean Theorem Proving by Filippo A. E. Nuccio.
